title: Stock Accuracy and Valuation
subtitle: Why quantities and values drift apart, and how to make counting boring
outcomes: Read the Stock Ledger and explain any valuation you see
Choose and defend a valuation method
Run cycle counts with Stock Reconciliation instead of destructive edits
Trace batches and serials end to end

slides.title: Every movement is one row
bullets: Each receipt, issue, transfer and count writes a Stock Ledger Entry with quantity, rate, value and a running balance
Valuation rate is derived, not typed: it follows the method and the order of entries
Back-dating a movement recalculates later balances — that is 'reposting', and it is normal, not corruption
The Stock and Account Value Difference is the diagnostic: if it is not zero, stock and the ledger disagree
slides.notes: Show the Stock Ledger report live and read a row out loud: posting date, item, warehouse, quantity change, valuation rate, balance quantity, balance value. Everything else in inventory accounting is a consequence of that row. When someone claims stock is wrong, ask which row they think is wrong and why, and the conversation becomes specific within a minute.

callout.title: The one report to trust
callout.text: Stock Ledger, filtered to one item and warehouse, sorted by date. If the ledger is right, the balances it produces are right.

slides.title: FIFO or Moving Average — pick once
bullets: FIFO consumes the oldest layers first: outbound valuation reflects historical purchase prices
Moving Average re-averages on every receipt: outbound valuation follows the blended cost
FIFO suits commodities and price-volatile goods; moving average suits stable, high-volume trading
Changing the method on live data requires a stock reposting and changes every historical margin — decide in the pilot
slides.notes: Both methods are legitimate; inconsistency is not. The choice affects gross margin, tax provisioning and how a purchasing win shows up in the P&L. Document the decision with a sentence of justification, because the first auditor question will be why. If you must change later, treat it as an accounting policy change with a repost, a disclosure and a lot of testing on a copy.

rows: Outbound cost tracks actual layers bought
Fast-moving retail with many small receipts
Component costs blend across production runs

slides.title: Stock Entry types, and the ones that should be rare
bullets: Material Receipt, Material Issue, Material Transfer (with or without transit), Manufacture, Repack
Use transfers for movement between warehouses, never a receipt plus an issue — that invents stock in and out
Opening stock is a Material Receipt flagged 'Opening Stock' so reports can separate it from trading
Material Issue is for consumption; an unexplained issue is usually a missing bill of materials or a write-off
slides.notes: Stock Entry is the escape hatch of inventory, and escape hatches attract mess. Set a rule: any stock entry that is not a transfer or an opening balance needs a reason in the remarks and a named approver. Then read the remarks column monthly; it is the cheapest audit you will ever run.

slides.title: Stock Reconciliation: how to be wrong safely
bullets: Enter the counted quantity and the valuation rate; ERPNext posts the difference to the difference account
Count in cycles — a rolling subset weekly — rather than an annual shutdown that freezes operations
Reconcile per warehouse and per batch; one reconciliation per item avoids double-posting the same variance
Never fix a count by editing old receipts: the variance is a fact, and the ledger should show it
slides.notes: Counting is a control, not a correction. If the same item is always short, the count is telling you about theft, breakage or an unrecorded issue — investigate the cause before adjusting the number. Keep the reconciliation documents: they are the evidence that a variance was approved rather than discovered.

callout.title: Expense vs stock adjustment
callout.text: Point the difference account at 'Stock Adjustment' for small variances and at an expense account for write-offs. Mixing them hides shrinkage inside cost of goods sold.

slides.title: Batches, serials and expiry
bullets: Enable batch or serial tracking on the item; batch numbers are needed for expiry reports and recalls
Serial numbers are individual units: one row per unit, with warranty and asset links if used
'Has Expiry Date' plus shelf life in days drives the Batch Expiry report and automatic batch selection
Traceability is only as good as discipline at receipt — a batch scanned late breaks the whole chain
slides.notes: Regulated industries do not get to skip this. In food, pharma and electronics, a recall costs more than the whole ERP project. Practise a mock recall once: pick a batch number and prove you can list every customer it reached. If that takes a day, fix the process now, when nobody is watching.
paths: Stock > Stock Settings > Enable Serial and Batch

slides.title: Landed cost, reposting and the value difference
bullets: Landed Cost Voucher distributes freight, duty and insurance across received items and posts the offset to a clearing or expense account
Repost Item Valuation recalculates historical entries after a back-dated movement or a corrected rate
Reposting is expensive on large histories: run it off-peak and check the progress log
If stock and accounting disagree, compare the Stock and Account Value Difference report before touching anything
slides.notes: Most 'the stock value is wrong' tickets resolve to one of three causes: a receipt at the wrong rate, a landed cost never applied, or a repost that is still queued. Diagnose in that order. Do not start editing entries; you will multiply the problem and lose the evidence.

callout.title: Repost queue
callout.text: Repost Item Valuation runs in the background. A stuck queue silently freezes valuation corrections — check its status after every correction.

slides.title: Warehouses, transit and inter-company
bullets: Model physical reality: one leaf warehouse per location where stock physically sits; group warehouses only for reporting
Transit warehouses hold goods between sites so in-transit value is visible instead of vanishing
Inter-company transfers need mirrored documents in both companies, or the group balance sheet will not eliminate
Warehouse-level permissions restrict who can see or move stock, and they apply to reports as well
slides.notes: Warehouse structure is the skeleton of every stock report. Two rules avoid most pain: a group warehouse never holds stock, and a transfer never changes company without a mirror document. If the group needs consolidation, build it from the company tree in ERPNext, not from spreadsheets.

slides.title: Scanning, mobile counting and the human layer
bullets: Barcodes remove the transcription errors that cause most stock variance; a scanner is cheaper than one recount
This repository's mobile inventory PWA scans codes and posts receipts, issues, transfers and counts offline, syncing when connectivity returns
Offline queues must be idempotent: the app stamps a marker in the document so a retry cannot double-post
Give the person counting a device and a basket, not a spreadsheet and hope
slides.notes: Warehouse software fails when it assumes connectivity. A phone that loses signal in a freezer should keep working and sync later; that is precisely what the bundled PWA was built for. Test any mobile flow by putting the device in flight mode halfway through and watching what happens to the queue.

lab.title: Count a cycle, transfer through transit, trace a batch
steps: Create two leaf warehouses plus a transit warehouse; move 10 units between them with a Stock Entry using the transit warehouse and inspect the two ledger rows
Receive 50 units of a batch-tracked item with an expiry date, then issue 5 to a customer and note the batch on the delivery note
Run a Stock Reconciliation counting 47 units on hand; post the variance to a stock adjustment account and read the ledger row
Back-date a receipt by one week and run Repost Item Valuation; compare the valuation before and after
Open Stock and Account Value Difference for the company and confirm it is zero, then explain what a non-zero value would mean
Produce the Batch Expiry report and the Stock Ageing report; identify one item that is ageing faster than it sells
lab.done: The ledger tells a coherent story: transfer in transit, batch traceable to a customer, variance posted as a document, and no value difference.

quiz.question: What does a Stock Ledger Entry store besides the quantity?
options: The valuation rate, value change and running balance
quiz.why: Valuation rate, value and running balances are on the entry, which is why inventory value can be reconstructed from the ledger.

quiz.question: You must move 10 units from Warehouse A to B. Which is correct?
options: A Material Issue from A and a Material Receipt to B
A Stock Reconciliation in both warehouses
quiz.why: A transfer keeps one movement with both sides linked. Issue plus receipt invents trading activity and breaks value continuity.

quiz.question: A physical count finds 47 units where the ledger says 50. What is the correct action?
options: Post a Stock Reconciliation for 47 with the variance to an adjustment account
Delete three units from the delivery note
Create a journal entry with no stock document
quiz.why: The variance is a real event. Reconciliation records it with an approver and leaves the history intact.

quiz.question: Stock quantity looks right but the balance sheet inventory value does not. Which report do you open first?
quiz.why: It compares the stock ledger's value to the GL inventory accounts and localises the discrepancy to items and warehouses.

quiz.question: Which practice most reliably prevents stock shrinkage from being hidden in cost of goods sold?
options: Separate adjustment and write-off accounts, reviewed monthly with reasons recorded
quiz.why: Separate accounts make shrinkage visible and reviewable; a single difference account quietly folds it into margin.

narration: Chapter five is stock accuracy, and it starts with one row. Every receipt, issue, transfer and count writes a stock ledger entry with quantity, valuation rate, value and a running balance. Everything else is a consequence. If someone says stock is wrong, ask which row is wrong. Valuation method is a policy decision. FIFO consumes the oldest layers, so cost of goods sold follows historical purchase prices. Moving average re-blends on every receipt, which smooths margins. Both are fine; inconsistency is not, and changing later requires a repost that rewrites history, so decide in the pilot. Use transfers for movement between warehouses, never a receipt plus an issue, because that invents trading activity. Opening stock is a receipt flagged as opening. When counts disagree, post a stock reconciliation with the counted quantity and send the difference to an adjustment account. Never edit old receipts to hide a variance, and keep adjustment and write-off accounts separate, otherwise shrinkage disappears into cost of goods sold and nobody investigates. For traceability, enable batches and serials at receipt time, because a batch scanned late breaks the chain; practise one mock recall. Finally, check the stock and account value difference report before any correction. If it is not zero, look for a wrong receipt rate, a missing landed cost, or a repost still queued.
